profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a public company, ticker NVDA, with CIK 0001045810. It was founded in 1993 and is headquartered in Santa Clara, California. Its most recent annual filing, a 10-K, reports revenue of $215,938,000,000. A litigation record associated with the company lists 281 cases in California.

On its site, NVIDIA describes the NVIDIA Nemotron family as multimodal, open AI models built for long-running, self-evolving agents, delivering agentic reasoning for graduate-level science, advanced math, and visual understanding. It says the models are openly available with transparent training data and broad platform support, including NVIDIA RTX PRO and NVIDIA DGX Spark. Named parts of the family include NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, NeMo Switchyard, Nemotron Speech models for automatic speech recognition, text-to-speech, and neural machine translation, and Nemotron Retriever models for document understanding. NVIDIA says it publishes model weights, training datasets, and training techniques, and offers the NVIDIA Open Model License, which it describes as permissive and as allowing use, modification, distribution, and commercial deployment without crediting NVIDIA. The page cites Bryan Catanzaro, VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA.

The Nemotron models are also offered as NVIDIA NIM microservices, which the company says require an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license and can be tried or downloaded from build.nvidia.com. NVIDIA lists NVIDIA NeMo, NVIDIA Blueprints, NVIDIA Dynamo, and TensorRT-LLM as tools for building and running the models at scale, along with the open-source libraries SGLang and vLLM. It says it works with partners across the ecosystem, including model builders and AI-native companies, and cites what ServiceNow discovered about visual question-answering accuracy.
